node.label: Robert Bartlett
node.description: A medieval historian of conquest, law and historical categories. Trial by Fire and Water (1986) studied the medieval judicial ordeal, and The Making of Europe (1993) traced conquest, colonization and cultural change between 950 and 1350. His 2001 article on race and ethnicity treats both terms as social constructions and warns against using present administrative labels as ready-made historical explanations. Comparing medieval terminology, he emphasizes culture, law, language and religion in the making of identities, while examining genealogical idioms of descent, and separates collective identity from any automatic demand for sovereign statehood. Geraldine Heng later questions the sharpness of his distinction between medieval cultural difference and biological racism.
